measures.title: Average monthly rent
measures.source: CMHC Rental Market Survey via Statistics Canada 34-10-0133
measures.universe: Privately initiated row and apartment structures with three or more rental units, in centres of 10,000+ people. October survey.
measures.notes: Nominal dollars for the existing rental stock, sitting tenants included; not asking rents for vacant units. Average rents move with the mix of units surveyed. Survey areas are redrawn after each Census.

measures.title: Average monthly rent, inflation-adjusted
measures.source: Derived: 34-10-0133 rent x provincial all-items CPI (18-10-0005)
measures.universe: As average monthly rent.
measures.notes: Rent in latest-year dollars using the all-items CPI of the centre's province (the first-named province for areas that cross a boundary). No value where the provincial CPI is not published.

measures.title: Change in average rent from the previous year
measures.universe: As average monthly rent.
measures.notes: Change between consecutive October surveys, nominal. Changes the year after a survey-area redraw partly reflect the new boundaries. Only computed where both years are published.

measures.title: Rental vacancy rate
measures.source: CMHC Rental Market Survey via Statistics Canada 34-10-0130 and 34-10-0131
measures.universe: Privately initiated row and apartment structures with three or more units; all bedroom sizes; metro areas and agglomerations of 50,000+.
measures.notes: Units vacant and available for immediate rental in October. Where an area is in both tables, the metro-area table is used.

measures.title: Consumer Price Index
measures.source: Statistics Canada 18-10-0005, annual average
measures.universe: Canada, provinces, Whitehorse, Yellowknife, Iqaluit and selected cities.
measures.notes: The rent index tracks the price of the same rental units over time, so it rises more slowly than average rent when new, dearer units enter the stock. Index levels compare a place with itself over time, not places with each other.

measures.title: Rent prices relative to all prices
measures.source: Derived: 18-10-0005 rent index / all-items index x 100
measures.universe: As the Consumer Price Index.
measures.notes: 100 in 2002. Above 100 means rent prices have risen faster than prices in general since 2002 in that place.

measures.title: Rent price inflation
measures.universe: As the Consumer Price Index.
measures.notes: Change in the annual-average rent index from the previous year.

measures.title: Median after-tax income
measures.source: Canadian Income Survey via Statistics Canada 11-10-0190
measures.universe: Economic families and persons not in an economic family; owners and renters together.
measures.notes: Constant dollars of the table's latest year. Not renter income: tenure is not a dimension of this table. Pre-2012 years come from earlier surveys revised to be comparable.

measures.title: Population
measures.source: Statistics Canada 17-10-0005 (provinces, from 1971) and 17-10-0148 (metro areas and agglomerations on 2021 boundaries, from 2001)
measures.universe: Population on July 1.
measures.notes: Estimates are revised as new Census results arrive.

measures.title: Housing starts
measures.source: CMHC Starts and Completions Survey via Statistics Canada 34-10-0126
measures.universe: All areas; provinces only (territories are not published).
measures.notes: Dwellings whose construction started that year, all tenures. Rental and ownership starts are not separated in this table.

measures.title: Housing completions
measures.source: CMHC Starts and Completions Survey via Statistics Canada 34-10-0126
measures.universe: All areas; provinces only.
measures.notes: Dwellings completed that year, all tenures.

measures.title: Housing starts per 1,000 residents
measures.universe: Provinces and Canada.
measures.notes: All starts divided by July 1 population.

measures.title: Apartments as a share of starts
measures.universe: Provinces and Canada.
measures.notes: Apartment and other unit types divided by all starts.

measures.title: Renters spending 30% or more of income on shelter, 2016 and 2021
measures.source: Statistics Canada, The Daily, 2022-09-21, table 4 (Census of Population)
measures.universe: Renter households with income above zero in non-farm, non-reserve private dwellings; 2016 and 2021 Censuses on 2021 boundaries.
measures.notes: Published to one decimal for Canada, every province and territory and 41 metro areas. Shelter costs are for the Census year, income for the year before; 2020 income includes pandemic benefits. This release can differ slightly from the detailed 2021 table; the two are never mixed in one series.

measures.title: Renters spending 30% or more of income on shelter, 2021
measures.source: 2021 Census, Statistics Canada 98-10-0252 (Canada, provinces, metros, agglomerations) and 98-10-0255 (divisions, communities)
measures.universe: Off-reserve renter households with income above zero in non-farm private dwellings; 25% sample.
measures.notes: Rate = households at 30%+ / (30%+ and under 30%); not-applicable households excluded. Counts are randomly rounded to multiples of 5, so rates for communities with few renters are unreliable; the page shows the renter count beside every community rate.

measures.title: Renter burden by household type, 2021
measures.source: 2021 Census, Statistics Canada 98-10-0252
measures.universe: As 2021 renter burden.
measures.notes: Family and non-family households are totals of the types under them. Couple and one-parent rows are households with no additional persons.

measures.title: Renter burden by household income, 2021
measures.source: 2021 Census, Statistics Canada 98-10-0252
measures.universe: As 2021 renter burden.
measures.notes: Household total income before tax in 2020.

measures.title: Renter burden in subsidized and market housing, 2021
measures.source: 2021 Census, Statistics Canada 98-10-0255
measures.universe: As 2021 renter burden, split by whether the rent is subsidized (rent geared to income, social or non-profit housing, rent supplements, housing allowances).
measures.notes: Subsidized households can still spend 30%+ where the subsidy is not geared to income.

measures.title: Households that rent, 2021
measures.source: 2021 Census, Statistics Canada 98-10-0255
measures.universe: Off-reserve private households in non-farm private dwellings.
measures.notes: Renter households / all households, including households outside the burden universe. Communities on reserve have no off-reserve households and show no value.

measures.title: Renters in subsidized housing, 2021
measures.source: 2021 Census, Statistics Canada 98-10-0255
measures.universe: Off-reserve renter households in non-farm private dwellings.
measures.notes: Subsidized renter households / all renter households.

measures.title: Renter households, 2021
measures.source: 2021 Census, Statistics Canada 98-10-0255
measures.universe: Off-reserve renter households in non-farm private dwellings.
measures.notes: Randomly rounded to a multiple of 5.

measures.title: Renters in core housing need

cats.market: Not in social and affordable housing

measures.source: Canadian Housing Survey via Statistics Canada 46-10-0085
measures.universe: Renter households in the provinces; the territories are surveyed separately and are not in this table. 'Canada' means the ten provinces.
measures.notes: A household is in core housing need when its dwelling is unaffordable, crowded or needs major repairs and acceptable local housing would cost 30%+ of its income. Not the same as spending 30%+. Survey years 2018, 2021, 2022, 2024; nothing is drawn between them. 95% confidence intervals shown.

measures.title: Housing standards renters fall below
measures.source: Canadian Housing Survey via Statistics Canada 46-10-0086
measures.universe: Renter households in core housing need, provinces.
measures.notes: Affordability: shelter costs 30%+ of before-tax income. Suitability: not enough bedrooms. Adequacy: major repairs needed.

measures.title: Renters in core housing need by community size
measures.source: Canadian Housing Survey via Statistics Canada 46-10-0085
measures.universe: Renter households in the provinces, grouped by population-centre size.
measures.notes: Not every province has every size class.
